blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Smart Home Installation Cost in South Melbourne in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking about a smart home in South Melbourne? We break down the costs for lighting, blinds, security, and whole-home automation in 2026.
body: Smart home automation isn't just for tech enthusiasts anymore. In South Melbourne, more homeowners are adding smart lighting, motorised blinds, and voice-controlled security to their terrace houses and apartments. But the big question is always: how much does it actually cost? The short answer is somewhere between $2,000 and $15,000, depending on how deep you go. A basic smart lighting setup for a three-bedroom home with dimmers and smart switches will set you back around $2,500 to $4,000 installed. That includes the wiring, the switches, and programming the app. If you want voice control through Google Home or Alexa, add a few hundred more for compatible hubs. For a full automation package — lights, blinds, heating and cooling, security cameras, and whole-home audio — you're looking at $8,000 to $15,000 in a typical South Melbourne home. The price jumps if you're doing a heritage property with solid brick walls, where running new cables is trickier. Wireless options exist but can be less reliable.

The biggest cost driver is the amount of rewiring required. Older homes in South Melbourne often have switchboards that can't handle modern loads. You might need a switchboard upgrade (around $1,200 to $2,000) before any smart system goes in. That's actually a good thing — a modern switchboard with safety switches is essential. Another factor is how many rooms you want automated. Doing the living areas only keeps the price down, but once you add bedrooms, outdoor spaces, and the kitchen, the labour and materials add up. We always recommend starting with a free on-site consultation. Our team at Platinum Electrical walks through your home, checks the existing wiring, and gives you a fixed quote. No guessing, no hidden fees. Smart home gear prices have dropped in the last few years, but installation labour still makes up the bulk. Expect around $200 to $300 per room for basic smart switch wiring, more if you need motorised blinds or sensors.

Is it worth the money for South Melbourne homeowners? In our experience, yes. Smart homes increase property value — especially in the inner south where buyers expect modern conveniences. They also save energy. Smart thermostats and automated blinds can cut heating and cooling costs by 20-30%. Plus, you get peace of mind with remote security monitoring. If you're in South Melbourne, Port Melbourne, or St Kilda, and thinking about automation, give us a call. We'll design a system that fits your budget and your lifestyle. And remember: always use a licensed electrician for any wiring work. DIY smart home gear can be dangerous and might void your insurance.

blogPosts.title: Gas to Electric Conversion: Is It Worth It for South Melbourne Homes in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of ditching gas? We explore the costs, rebates, and benefits of switching to electric appliances for your home in South Melbourne.
body: Victoria is slowly moving away from gas. New homes in some areas are being built all-electric, and the state government is offering incentives for existing homes to make the switch. For South Melbourne households, converting from gas to electric can mean lower energy bills, a smaller carbon footprint, and a safer home. But it's not a decision to make lightly. The upfront cost can be significant, especially if you need to upgrade your switchboard or run new circuits. A typical conversion includes replacing a gas cooktop with induction, swapping a gas hot water system for a heat pump, and changing gas heating to a reverse-cycle split system. Each appliance comes with its own installation cost. Induction cooktops range from $800 to $3,000, plus installation and potentially a new circuit. Heat pump hot water systems cost between $2,500 and $4,500 installed. Split system air conditioners vary by size but budget $2,000 to $5,000 per unit.

The good news is there are generous rebates available in 2026. The Victorian Energy Upgrades program can cover part of the cost for heat pumps and efficient appliances. The Solar Homes program also offers interest-free loans for solar and battery systems. You might also qualify for a gas disconnect rebate from the state government. In total, a full conversion from gas to electric for an average South Melbourne home could cost $8,000 to $15,000, but after rebates you might save $2,000 to $4,000. Over time, you'll save on gas supply charges and the cost per kilowatt-hour of electricity is typically lower than gas for heating. Induction cooking is faster and more precise, and reverse-cycle heating/cooling is efficient year-round.

One thing to keep in mind: your home's electrical capacity. Many older South Melbourne properties have 63 amp switchboards that can't handle the extra load. Upgrading to a 100 amp board with safety switches might add $2,000 to the bill. But it's worth it for safety and future-proofing. We've done dozens of gas-to-electric conversions across South Melbourne, Richmond, and Yarraville. The process usually takes a few days, and we coordinate with gas plumbers for the disconnect and capping. Our advice: get a full site assessment first. We'll check your switchboard, measure your cooking and heating needs, and give you a fixed quote including all rebate paperwork. Going all-electric is a smart move for the environment and your hip pocket.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Electrical Safety Checks Every South Melbourne Homeowner Should Do
blogPosts.excerpt: Keep your family safe with these essential electrical safety checks. Plus, what to look for in older homes across South Melbourne and Port Melbourne.
body: Electrical safety is something most homeowners don't think about until something goes wrong. In older South Melbourne homes — many built in the 1950s or earlier — the wiring can be outdated and dangerous. We recommend doing these five checks at least once a year. First: test your safety switches (RCDs). Every switchboard should have at least one RCD. Press the test button monthly; if it doesn't trip, call an electrician immediately. Second: look for old wiring. If you see cloth-insulated wiring, ceramic fuses, or black rubber cabling, that's a red flag. Homes built before 1970 often have wiring that can't handle modern appliances. A full rewiring costs $5,000 to $12,000 but it's non-negotiable for safety. Third: check your power points. Loose sockets, discolouration, or burning smells mean urgent repair. Fourth: inspect outdoor power points. They should be weatherproof and have a cover. Exposed outlets near pools, gardens, or patios are a shock risk. Fifth: make sure your smoke alarms are less than 10 years old and interconnected.

In South Melbourne, we also see a lot of DIY electrical work — people adding power points or light fixtures without a license. This is illegal and dangerous. Faulty wiring causes thousands of house fires each year in Victoria. If you've just bought an older home, or if you're planning renovations, get a full electrical safety inspection. It costs around $300 to $500 and covers the switchboard, wiring, earthing, smoke alarms, and RCDs. We include a detailed report with photos and a quote for any repairs needed. Many insurance companies now require an electrical safety certificate before they'll cover older homes. Don't skip it.

Another common issue in South Melbourne: DIYers have used mismatched wiring colours or joined cables with tape instead of junction boxes. These are fire hazards. If you notice flickering lights, buzzing sounds, or a tingling sensation when touching appliances, call a licensed electrician immediately. At Platinum Electrical, we offer priority emergency inspections across the inner south. We'll find the problem and fix it fast. Safety first, always. And remember: never overload power boards with heaters or air conditioners. Plug high-wattage appliances directly into wall sockets.

blogPosts.title: Complete Guide to Solar Panel Installation in South Melbourne (2026 Update)
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking about solar for your South Melbourne home? Here's everything you need to know about costs, rebates, and finding the right installer.
body: Solar power is more accessible than ever for South Melbourne homeowners. With rising electricity prices and generous federal and state incentives, installing solar panels can slash your power bills by 50-80%. A standard 6.6kW system — the most common size for a three-bedroom home — costs between $4,000 and $7,000 after the STC rebate. That's the Small-scale Technology Certificate discount applied upfront by reputable installers. For a larger 10kW system, expect $7,000 to $10,000. The payback period is usually 3 to 5 years in Victoria, thanks to our high feed-in tariffs. After that, you're essentially getting free electricity for the remaining 20+ years of the panels' life. South Melbourne gets decent sun exposure — even with Melbourne's variable weather, a well-oriented north-facing roof can generate enough power to cover most of your daytime usage.

Choosing the right installer is crucial. Make sure they are CEC (Clean Energy Council) accredited and use Tier 1 solar panels. Cheap systems using poor-quality panels will degrade faster and won't save you as much in the long run. We use brands like Jinko, Trina, and Longi, paired with Fronius or Sungrow inverters. Battery storage is becoming more popular too. A 5kWh battery adds about $8,000 to $10,000 to the system cost, but it lets you store excess solar energy for use at night. With the Victorian Solar Battery Rebate, you might get up to $4,800 off. For South Melbourne homes with limited roof space, we also offer microinverters that maximise energy harvest even when parts of the roof are shaded. We always do a full site inspection to design the best layout for your roof pitch and orientation.

Planning permission is straightforward in South Melbourne. Most residential solar installations are covered under exempt development as long as they don't protrude more than 10cm above the roofline. Your installer should handle all the paperwork, including the connection application to your electricity distributor. Once installed, a 6.6kW system can save around $1,300 per year on an average bill. Combine it with a heat pump hot water system and induction cooking, and you could almost eliminate your energy costs. We've installed over 500 solar systems across South Melbourne, Port Melbourne, and St Kilda. Give us a call for a free quote and we'll walk you through the numbers.
